newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas prices soften ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices soften ahead of weekend.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for June extended their losses Friday as the futures market tumbled and mild weather blanketed the West, industry sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, June prices slipped about six cents to C$1.50-C$1.52 per gigajoule, while next-day prices were quoted at C$1.49-C$1.50.

Temperatures in Calgary, Alberta, were forecast to reach highs in the low-70s Fahrenheit on Saturday, followed by a high of about 66 degrees on Sunday, Weather Services Corp reported. July Hub futures fell to a low of $2.20, down five cents.
"It was on the heels of NYMEX going down again. There aren't many fundamental reasons. It's pretty quiet," one Calgary-based trader said, referring to Alberta pricing.

Also feeling the brunt of technical selling on NYMEX was the Niagara market, where most deals were reported done around $2.40-$2.41 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), down three cents from on Thursday.

Canadian Gas Association (CGA) said Friday that eastern stocks as of May 23 were at 28.17 bcf, or 12.1 percent, compared with 11.5 percent full a year ago. Overall stocks were at 105.5 bcf, or 21.5 percent full. These data compare with year-ago tallies at 26.3 percent full.
At Sumas, Wash., June gas traded about two cents lower at $1.20-$1.25 per mmBtu.
CGA also said that gas stocks in the West were at 77.33 bcf as of May 23, or 29.8 percent full, compared with 38.6 percent full a year ago.
